editorial_czech.text: Tisícerý dík, Aničko moje líbezná, za včerejší lístek, který dodán byl teprve [odpoledne?] za mé nepřítomnosti. Jak mohla se domysleti, že mne [korespondence?] s ní omrzela? Vždyť se vždy na její drahé řádky tak toužebně těším. Vždyť také já mám tě, Aničko moje jediná, tak z celé, vřelé duše, tak vášnivě rád. Hlavička, moje zlato, již nebolí, za to však srdéčko velice po [tobě?] stůně. Jsi ty též [alternativa: teď?] zase úplně zdráva. Nenachladila se mi na ledě. Tisíc vřelých dlouhých, vášnivých pus posílá ti [věčně?] tvůj Pepouš.

Written line-end hyphens may be joined; such joins are not cipher evidence. Ciphertext and literal lines remain unchanged.

english_translation.text: A thousand thanks, my lovely Anička, for yesterday’s note, which was delivered only in the [afternoon?] during my absence. How could she imagine that [correspondence?] with her had become tiresome to me? I always look forward so eagerly to her dear lines. I too love you, my only Anička, with all my warm soul, so passionately. The little head, my darling, no longer hurts, but my heart aches very much for [you?]. You are also [alternative: now?] completely well again. She has not caught cold on the ice, to my concern [literal wording remains unusual]. A thousand warm, long, passionate kisses are sent to you [forever?] by your Pepouš.
english_translation.basis: Translation of the editorial proposal, not of a certified source transcription; bracketed or explicitly labeled alternatives carry restoration uncertainty.
